Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call: 1 of 5 (sonnet-2). The deciding sentence is "A shorter literal that fits its line stays on one line." Sonnet-2 lines 119-124 spread a four-element table_options list one option per line, where the one-line form would be 82 characters. Haiku-1 (lines 88-94) and sonnet-1 (lines 133-139) name the same kind of list one option per line where one line would be 106 and 110 characters, so the sentence allows it; opus-1 line 173 and haiku-2 lines 102 and 105 keep short lists inline on one line. The more-than-six-elements sentence is not triggered (no literal has more than six elements), no run passes a multi-line map or struct to a call, and the trailing-keyword-list sentence is not reached (no unbound call takes a multi-line keyword list). This is a judgment call worth a ruling: the processes.md example that every run read ("Use ETS for data many processes read") writes a five-element table_options list one option per line whose one-line form is exactly 98 characters, so the skill's own example shows the layout the sentence forbids. Reading the sentence as permissive only, as the 2026-10-29-check ecto-phoenix grade did, makes sonnet-2 clean and the count 0 of 5.

Chain fallible steps with `with`: 0 of 5. The deciding sentences are "A `with` chains two or more `<-` steps. One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail and there is no `else`, so the `with` does nothing but pass the error through; any other one-step `with` is a `case`." and "A body that is one call whose `{:ok, value}` or `{:error, reason}` goes out as the function's own result ... is a tail call, not a second step". Opus-1 (lines 203-206) and sonnet-1 (lines 190-193) chain two steps and end in a tail call to parse_limits/1 or validate_limits/1, which is not a third step; their init/1 case statements (opus-1 line 169, sonnet-1 line 131) turn the error into {:stop, ...}, so they are not the pass-through case the rule turns into a with. Haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 read their files with raising boot-time calls and have no with and no tuple-returning step, so they are not exercised, as in 2026-10-23. No run writes a pass-through case or a one-step with.

Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance; otherwise put each body on its own line: 0 of 5; exercised in four runs, not in haiku-1 (no case, cond, receive, with ... else or fn in code). The deciding sentences are "A clause of `case`, `cond`, `receive`, `with ... else` or a multi-clause `fn` stays on one line when the clauses form a table, or when each body is one expression simple enough to take in together with its pattern", the 70-character sentence, and "when one clause breaks, every clause of that `case` does, with a blank line between clauses". The one-line clauses in code are all within 70 after indentation: opus-1 lines 213-214 (46, 47), haiku-2 lines 120-121 (29, 53) and sonnet-1 lines 179-180 (24, 44), the last two the ETS lookup table the rule itself shows. Every case with a multi-expression clause is broken as a whole with blank lines between (opus-1 lines 169-179; sonnet-1 lines 131-148, 197-203, 207-213). Under the current text a single-clause fn argument is governed too ("A single-clause `fn` passed as an argument reads the same way: one expression stays on its line, more goes below."), where the check batches left fn arguments outside the rule; sonnet-1 lines 185 and 218 and sonnet-2 line 142 each hold one expression and are clean, which is what makes sonnet-2 exercised. Following 2026-10-23-check-2 and later, clauses inside @moduledoc examples are not counted; the one over 70 there is sonnet-1 line 73 ({:error, {:rate_limited, retry_after_ms}} -> {:snooze, div(retry_after_ms, 1000) + 1}, 85 characters, beside a one-line :ok clause). No run calls Jason, so no Jason compile warning arises.

Designs. All five keep one ETS row per admitted request in a public ordered_set table owned by a GenServer; the caller inserts its row, counts the user's rows from the last minute with :ets.select_count/2 and deletes its row when over the limit; a handle_info/2 sweep every minute deletes expired rows with :ets.select_delete/2. No run has handle_call/3 or cast. Limits live in :persistent_term (opus-1, haiku-1, sonnet-2), in a second protected table (haiku-2) or as rows in the same table (sonnet-1). Opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 read JSON with JSON.decode or :json.decode and normalize user IDs to strings; sonnet-2 evaluates an Elixir script with Code.eval_file/1 (which runs whatever code the file holds) and keys limits and counts by the raw user ID, so 42 and "42" are different users, as its moduledoc's string keys imply. Sonnet-1 returns a retry time with the refusal. Haiku-2 registers name: __MODULE__ with fixed table names, so no second instance can start.
